title: The Tale of the Fifth Brother, the Cropped of Ears

paragraphs.en: My fifth brother, the cropped of ears, was a poor beggar. After our father's death, he received one hundred dirhams from the inheritance. Initially unsure how to use this money, he decided to buy glass and sell it for profit.
paragraphs.zh: 我的五弟，缺耳的，原本是个穷困潦倒的乞丐。父亲过世后，他从遗产中分得了一百第纳尔。起初他对这笔钱如何使用有些犹豫不决，最终决定买些玻璃制品，转手倒卖以图盈利。

paragraphs.en: He purchased a hundred dirhams' worth of glass and placed it in a large basket. Sitting next to a tailor’s shop with a balustrade at the entrance, he leaned against it, dreaming aloud.
paragraphs.zh: 他买了一百迪拉姆的玻璃，放在一个大篮子里。坐在一家裁缝店旁，门口有栏杆，他倚着栏杆，自言自语地做起梦来。

paragraphs.en: "I will start with one hundred dirhams," he thought, "and double my capital by selling the glass for two hundred dirhams. With that money, I'll buy more glass and sell it for four hundred dirhams. This process will continue until I have ten thousand dirhams, then forty thousand, and eventually a hundred thousand dirhams.
paragraphs.zh: 他心想，先拿出一百迪尔汗作为本金，然后把玻璃卖两百迪尔汗翻一番。用这笔钱再买进更多的玻璃，转手卖出就能赚到四百迪尔汗。这个过程会一直持续下去，直到积累到一万、四万，最终达到十万迪尔汗。

paragraphs.en: With such wealth, I can buy jewels, perfumes, and a fine house with slaves and horses. I’ll live in luxury, feasting and enjoying the company of singers."
paragraphs.zh: 有了这么多财富，我可以买珠宝、香水和一座带奴隶和马匹的豪华宅邸。我将过着奢侈的生活，尽情享受歌姬们的陪伴。

paragraphs.en: He sat there, lost in his ambitious thoughts, unaware that his future lay ahead.
paragraphs.zh: 他坐在那里，沉浸在他的雄心壮志中，全然不知自己的未来就在前方。

paragraphs.en: He sat with his thoughts, staring at the basket filled with one hundred dirhams worth of glass. He mused aloud, "Once I have amassed a hundred thousand dirhams, I'll seek marriage for myself among the daughters of kings and viziers. The vizier's daughter, they say, is exceptionally beautiful—perfection itself.
paragraphs.zh: 他坐在那里沉思，盯着篮子里装着价值一百迪拉姆的玻璃珠子。他不禁出声自语：“等我攒够十万迪拉姆，我就去寻找王公贵族的女儿作为妻子。据说宰相的女儿尤为美丽——简直是完美无瑕。”

paragraphs.en: I will offer her a dowry of one thousand dinars. If she refuses, I'll take her by force. Upon my return, I'll buy ten slaves and fine clothes, and commission a golden saddle adorned with jewels.
paragraphs.zh: 我将给她一千第纳尔作为嫁妆。如果她拒绝，我就强行娶她。等我回来后，我会买十个奴隶和一些华贵的衣裳，并定制一具镶满宝石的金鞍。

paragraphs.en: I'll parade through the city, with slaves in front and behind, as people greet me and bless me. When I meet the vizier, he will rise to greet me, seating me above him because of our impending marriage. I'll bring two slaves carrying one thousand dinars each—half for the dowry, half as a gift—to demonstrate my generosity and disdain for worldly concerns.
paragraphs.zh: 我会在城中巡游，前面和后面都有奴隶跟随，人们向我致敬并为我祝福。当我遇见首相时，他会起身迎接，并因我们即将成婚而让我坐得比他高。我会带着两名奴隶，每人捧着一千第纳尔——一半作为嫁妆，另一半作为礼物，以此展示我的慷慨以及对世俗事务的不屑一顾。

paragraphs.en: Upon returning home, if someone brings a message from the bride, I'll give them money and a robe of honor. If they offer me a present, I'll return it to maintain my dignity. Then, I'll prepare my house and instruct them to ready the bride.
paragraphs.zh: 回到家后，如果有人带来新娘的消息，我会给他们一些钱和礼服。如果有礼物送给我，我会原物奉还以保全自己的尊严。随后，我会安排好家中事宜，并吩咐他们为新娘做好准备。

paragraphs.en: When she's prepared, I'll sit on a silk brocade seat, leaning on a cushion, not turning left or right out of propriety. The full moon will stand before me in her robes and ornaments. Out of self-respect, I won't look at her until everyone says, 'O our lord and master, your wife stands before you.
paragraphs.zh: 待她准备妥当，我将坐在绣花座垫上，倚靠其上，出于礼节不左顾右盼。满月将以她的华服盛装立于我面前。出于自尊，我不会看她一眼，直到所有人都说：“啊，我们的老爷，您的夫人站在您面前。”

paragraphs.en: Be kind to her.' After they kiss the ground many times, I'll raise my head, give her a glance, then lower it again. They will take her away, and I'll change into finer clothes.
paragraphs.zh: “对她好点儿。”说完这话，他们跪地拜了又拜。我这才抬起头瞥了一眼，随即又低下头去。接着他们会带走她，而我会换上更体面的衣服。

paragraphs.en: When she returns in her second dress, I won't look at her until they implore me repeatedly. Then, I'll give her a quick glance before looking down again, repeating this process until the display is complete."
paragraphs.zh: 当她第二次换上那套衣服回来时，我不会看她，直到他们一再恳求我才勉强瞥一眼，然后马上把目光移开。如此反复，直到整个展示结束。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad resumed her story on the following night. "My brother," she began, "planned to enjoy watching the bride until their presentation. Then he would order a servant to bring him five hundred dinars, which he would give to the bride's attendants.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹在第二天晚上继续讲述：“我的哥哥原本打算享受观看新娘直到婚礼当天，然后他会吩咐仆人给他带来五百第纳尔，再把这些钱交给新娘的侍女。

paragraphs.en: They were to lead him to the chamber where the bride awaited."
paragraphs.zh: 他们将带他前往新娘等候的房间。

paragraphs.en: "He would lie beside her without speaking, making it seem that she was proud and unapproachable," Shahrazad continued. "When her mother entered, she would kiss his hand and plead for his comfort. He would remain silent, causing her to kiss his feet repeatedly before offering him wine.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德接着说：“他会默默地躺在她身旁，仿佛她是高傲而难以接近的。”“当母亲进来时，她会吻他的手，乞求他宽慰。他依然沉默不语，让她不得不一次次亲吻他的脚踝，最终才端上酒来。”

paragraphs.en: He would let the bride stand while he reclined on a golden cushion, ignoring her completely."
paragraphs.zh: 他让自己靠在金垫子上，却让新娘站立着，完全不理她。

paragraphs.en: "Eventually, she would beg him to drink from the cup," Shahrazad said. "He would shake his fist at her and kick over a basket of glass, breaking everything inside."
paragraphs.zh: “最终，她会央求他喝酒。”莎赫拉兹说，“他会冲着她挥舞拳头，踢翻一篮子玻璃杯，把里面的东西全都打碎了。”

paragraphs.en: A tailor who overheard the fifth brother's self-talk exclaimed, "This pride of yours has brought you down. If it were in my power, I'd beat you a hundred times and parade you through the city." The brother then began beating his face, tearing his clothes, and weeping.
paragraphs.zh: 一个裁缝无意中听到了五弟的自言自语，不禁脱口而出：“你这傲气可真够呛，要是我有的话，非得好好教训你一百遍，让你在全城丢尽脸面。”随后，五弟开始打自己的脸，扯烂衣服，痛哭流涕。

paragraphs.en: Passersby saw him; some pitied him, others ignored him.
paragraphs.zh: 路人见了他，有的同情他的遭遇，有的则视而不见。

paragraphs.en: A beautiful lady on a golden-saddled she-mule passed by, her presence filling the air with musk. Seeing the brother weep, she inquired about him. Learning he had lost a basket of glass and was now destitute, she gave one of her servants instructions to give the brother five hundred dinars.
paragraphs.zh: 一位身骑金鞍母驴的美丽女士从他们身边经过，她的香气弥漫在空气中。见这位兄弟哭泣，她便询问起他来。得知他丢失了一篮子玻璃器皿，如今一贫如洗后，她吩咐一名仆人给这位兄弟五百第纳尔。

paragraphs.en: Overjoyed, the brother thanked the lady profusely.
paragraphs.zh: 兄长欣喜若狂，向那 lady 连声道谢。

paragraphs.en: Just then, there was a knock at his door. Rushing to open it, he found an old woman he did not recognize. She asked if she could perform ablutions in his house before prayer time.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，有人敲门。他急忙去开门，发现是一位不认识的老妇人。她询问是否可以在祈祷前在他家进行净身仪式。

paragraphs.en: The brother agreed and brought her a ewer for washing. As he stuffed the money into his clothes, the old woman prayed nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 兄弟应允了，拿来一只水罐让她洗手。他把钱塞进衣服里时，老妇人在旁边默默祈祷。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused. Dinarzad remarked on the story's strangeness, to which Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would tell the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹停下了讲述。丁纳扎德对这个故事感到有些诧异，沙赫拉兹则回应说，这比起她如果活下来将在明天晚上讲述的内容简直不值一提。

paragraphs.en: The old woman, after blessing the king, received two dinars from him as an offering. She then revealed that she knew of a wealthy and beautiful woman in the city. My brother was intrigued and followed her to a grand mansion.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人在祝福了国王后，收到了两枚第纳尔作为祭品。接着她透露自己知道城里有一位富有而美丽的女子。我的哥哥对此颇感兴趣，便跟随她来到了一座宏伟的府邸。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering, he saw a young lady dressed richly and found himself charmed.
paragraphs.zh: 一进门，他就见到一位穿着华丽的年轻女士，不禁为之倾心。

paragraphs.en: A Greek slave-girl opened the door, and the old woman led my brother into a spacious hall. He sat down, placed his money before him, and removed his turban, placing it on his knee. The young lady entered, her beauty captivating.
paragraphs.zh: 一个希腊籍的女奴开了门，老妇人领着我的哥哥走进了一个宽敞的大厅。他坐了下来，在面前放好钱，摘下了头巾，放在了膝上。那位年轻女士随后走了进来，她的美貌令人目不转睛。

paragraphs.en: She invited him to follow her to a private room where they dallied for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 她邀请他跟随她到了一个私密的房间，在那里他们闲聊了好一阵子。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a large black slave entered with a sword. He demanded what my brother was doing there. My brother was speechless.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，一个高大的黑奴手持利剑闯了进来，质问我的兄弟为何在此。我的兄弟一时语塞。

paragraphs.en: The slave stripped and struck him severely, leaving him half-paralyzed. The slave continued to strike until my brother fell unconscious. The slave then asked for salt from a maid, who brought it.
paragraphs.zh: 奴隶将他剥得赤裸，狠狠地打了他一顿，打得他半身不遂。奴隶继续施打，直到我的兄弟昏死过去。随后，奴隶向一名女仆要了些盐，女仆带来了盐。

paragraphs.en: He stuffed my brother's wounds with salt before he fainted again.
paragraphs.zh: 他在我哥哥伤口里撒满了盐，然后他又昏了过去。

paragraphs.en: When he regained consciousness, the fifth brother lay still out of fear. The maid left, and the black slave called for the cellar-woman. She arrived, dragging him down into a cellar filled with dead bodies.
paragraphs.zh: 当他恢复意识时，第五兄弟吓得一动不动。女仆离开了，那名黑奴喊来了看管地窖的妇人。她带着他来到了一个堆满了死尸的地窖里。

paragraphs.en: For two days, he remained unconscious until God's intervention stopped the bleeding due to salt. Once able to move, he cautiously escaped and hid in the hallway until morning. He returned home and treated himself for a month before fully recovering.
paragraphs.zh: 连续两天，他一直处于昏迷状态，直到上帝的干预才止住了因盐而引起的出血。恢复行动能力后，他小心翼地点逃了出来，藏在走廊里躲到天亮。回家后，他自我调养了一个月，这才完全康复。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, he kept an eye on the old woman as she led others into her house. However, he did not speak of his ordeal. After regaining strength, he sewed a bag from cloth and filled it with glass.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，他留意着那位老妇人将其他人领进了她的屋子。不过，他并没有提及自己的遭遇。恢复了些许力气后，他用布缝了一个袋子，并在里面装满了玻璃珠。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what a strange and engaging story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to tell you if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫札德停下了口。迪纳札德remarked道：“姐姐，这故事真是既奇异又引人入胜！”沙赫札德回答说：“等到明天夜晚再说吧；如果国王饶恕了我，我还有很多精彩的故事要告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: O happy King, I heard that the tailor told the king of China that the barber had shared with his guests what he had said to the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 幸福的国王啊，我听说裁缝曾向中国国王禀报，理发师在宴会上将他与哈里发对话的内容透露给了宾客。

paragraphs.en: He disguised himself as a Persian, tied a glass to his waist, and hid a sword under his clothes. Spotting an old woman, he approached her with a Persian accent, asking if she had scales large enough for five hundred dinars. She led him to the house where her daughter greeted them.
paragraphs.zh: 他乔装成波斯人，腰间系了一块玻璃板，身上藏了一把剑。发现一位老妇人后，他用波斯口音上前询问是否有一副足够五百第纳尔的鱼鳞。老妇带他们进了家门，她的女儿已在门口迎接。

paragraphs.en: After some time, the old woman left.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，老妇人离开了。

paragraphs.en: The cursed black slave entered with a bare sword and ordered my brother to rise. My brother struck the slave, severing his head. He dragged the body to the cellar and shouted for the salt-woman.
paragraphs.zh: 那个被诅咒的黑奴手持一把光剑闯了进来，命令我的兄弟起身。我兄弟一怒之下挥剑砍下了那黑奴的头颅，然后拖着尸体去了地窖，并大声喊叫盐婆过来。

paragraphs.en: The maid brought in a dish of salt but fled when she saw him holding a sword; he caught her and cut off her head.
paragraphs.zh: 女仆端来一碟盐，见他手持利剑便吓得逃走了；他一把抓住她，砍下了她的头颅。

paragraphs.en: He then asked the old woman where the cellar-woman was. When she appeared, my brother revealed his identity, accusing her of luring him there. Despite her pleas for mercy, he struck her with the sword, cutting her into pieces.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后问那老妇人，地窖女工在哪里。老妇人刚一出现，我哥哥便揭露了自己的身份，指控她诱骗自己来到这里。尽管老妇人苦苦求饶，他还是挥剑砍向她，将她分尸。

paragraphs.en: The young lady saw her brother and begged for mercy. He promised to spare her but asked about her past. She explained that she had been enslaved by a merchant, and an old woman had befriended her before inviting her to a wedding where she was seized by the black slave.
paragraphs.zh: 这位小姐见了哥哥，哀求他网开一面。哥哥答应饶她一命，但要她交代过去的事情。她解释说曾被一名商人家奴所困，后来一位老妇人与她结识，并邀请她参加婚礼，在那里她被黑奴抢走。

paragraphs.en: She claimed three years of captivity due to the old woman's treachery.
paragraphs.zh: 她指控老妇人出卖了她，要求赔偿三年的监禁之苦。

paragraphs.en: The brother inquired if the slave kept any money or possessions. The lady confirmed he did, showing several chests filled with purses. As they stood there, she instructed him to leave and bring men to carry the money away.
paragraphs.zh: 哥哥询问奴隶是否有存留的财物。女士确认他确实有，便展示了几个装满钱袋的箱子。就在他们站在那里时，她吩咐哥哥离开，并带人来搬走这些钱财。

paragraphs.en: He hired ten men but returned to find the door open and the lady gone, taking most of the money. Realizing her deception, he took what was left, carried away all the clothes, and left nothing behind. That night, they spent it happily.
paragraphs.zh: 他雇了十个人，结果回来却发现门大开，那位夫人已经不见踪影，还带走了大部分的钱。意识到自己的被骗后，他只拿了剩下的钱，连同所有的衣物一起带走，什么也没留下。那个晚上，他们过得非常愉快。

paragraphs.en: In the morning, twenty policemen arrived at his door. They seized him without delay and tied his hands behind his back. Despite offering money and pleading, they refused to let him enter his house before taking him away.
paragraphs.zh: 清晨，二十名警察敲开了他的门。他们毫不迟疑地将他抓走，并反绑了他的双手。尽管他掏出钱来央求，他们还是坚决不让他回家，直接带走了他。

paragraphs.en: On their way, a friend of my brother’s intervened, but the officers explained that they were following orders from the chief police officer.
paragraphs.zh: 途中，我哥哥的一个朋友试图干预，但那些军官解释说他们是在首席警官的命令下行动。

paragraphs.en: My brother clung to his friend, begging for help. The friend agreed to intercede, asking the officers if they could release him and inform their superior that he couldn't be found. However, the officers refused and dragged my brother face down towards the chief of police.
paragraphs.zh: 我的兄弟紧紧抓住他的朋友，央求帮助。朋友答应出面说情，请求那些军官释放他，并告知上级自己找不到人了。然而，军官们拒绝了，将我的兄弟拖倒在地，朝警长的方向走去。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "Sister, what a strange and entertaining story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if I stay alive to hear more."
paragraphs.zh: 天色渐亮，莎赫拉兹停下了讲述。丁纳兹说道：“姐姐，这故事真奇怪又有趣！”莎赫拉兹 aden：“如果我能活到明天晚上，你就能听到更多。”

paragraphs.en: My brother was summoned by the chief who asked about his possessions. My brother requested immunity first, which was granted. He then recounted his adventures with an old woman and the escape of a young lady.
paragraphs.zh: 我的哥哥被头领召见，询问了他的家产。哥哥首先请求豁免赋税，这一请求得到了许可。随后，他讲述了与一位老妇人的奇遇以及救出一位年轻女士的经历。

paragraphs.en: He assured the chief that he had kept what he took and offered to leave enough for himself.
paragraphs.zh: 他向长官保证自己已经妥善保管了所取之物，并提出留下足够的份额给自己。

paragraphs.en: However, the chief sent men to take all his money and clothes. Fearing the matter might reach the king, the chief ordered my brother to leave the city or face death. My brother obeyed and left for another city.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，首领派人将他所有的钱财和衣物都收走了。为了避免此事传到国王耳中，首领命令我的哥哥要么离开这座城市，要么面临死亡的威胁。哥哥听从了指示，前往另一个城市。

paragraphs.en: On his journey, some thieves attacked him, stripping him of his belongings. Upon hearing this, I took some clothes and followed him secretly. I clothed him and brought him back into the city to join his brothers.
paragraphs.zh: 在路上，一些盗贼袭击了他，抢走了他的财物。听到这个消息后，我拿了一些衣服悄悄跟着他。我给他穿上衣服，把他带回城里与兄弟们团聚。
